findings.criterion: [operator-attested] Direct Anthropic and Bedrock canaries pass with secrets absent from output and artifacts; the ticket records timestamp, model ids, request counts, cache read/write/input counts, complete/omit branch, and successful typed result.
findings.detail: The criterion is operator-attested and requires a concrete attestation with timestamp, model ids, request counts, cache read/write/input counts, complete/omit branch, and successful typed result. No such attestation is visible in the ticket snapshot I read. The ticket's own text explicitly states 'NO live call was made and this is NOT self-attested as passed' and the checkbox is unchecked [ ]. The ticket comment confirms: 'AC-6 left [operator-attested] unchecked per honest-attestation policy; a human operator with creds must run the cache canaries and record model ids + cache read/write/input counts + complete/omit branch on this ticket.'
findings.remediation: A credentialed human operator must run the direct Anthropic and Bedrock same-run cache canaries, then record a ticket comment naming: (1) timestamp of the run, (2) model ids used, (3) request counts, (4) cache read/write/input counts, (5) complete vs omit branch observed, and (6) the successful typed result returned. The comment must include these specific verifiable details to satisfy the operator-attested criterion.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[operator-attested]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
